description: Small pedestal-mounted spirit house shaped like a miniature temple with a tiered roof

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small pedestal-mounted spirit house shaped like a miniature temple with a tiered roof Materials: gilded paint over concrete, weathered gold leaf, mildew in the crevices.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 1,624/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/8 unique geometries, two 256 px canvases. The eave rebuild cost 224 triangles and no other axis; the horn taper and the heavier verdigris cost nothing on any of the four.

featureReviews.evidence: Ten-band proxy comparison: mean |delta w| 0.0054 and |delta d| 0.0047 of H, every one of the ten bands inside 0.015. The first build read 0.0386 / 0.0523 with all ten bands UNDER-width.
featureReviews.notes: Three faults, all measured, none of them surface: the declared envelope was 0.50 x 0.45 where the proxy needs 0.63 x 0.62 -- small enough that the model's own octagonal pedestal, at 0.551 m across, stood outside the envelope it was declared in; the roof eave was 0.520 across the flats where band 6 reads 0.442 H = 0.575; and the slab was one box, which cannot be both band 2 (0.555 m) and band 3 (0.434 m).

featureReviews.evidence: Eave plane 0.575 m across the flats (proxy band 6 = 0.442 H), concave flared profile to a ridge at 1.016, a second tier to 1.146, a lotus finial to 1.30. Bands 6 and 7 now +0.004 / +0.011 against -0.038 / -0.026.
featureReviews.notes: THE EAVE IS A CONTINUOUS ROLLED FASCIA, NOT FOUR CORNER STUBS. The plate (scratch/_horn.png, the plate's left eave corner at 3x) shows the eave EDGE dipping at mid-span and sweeping up into a point at each corner -- one curve, not a brim with horns bolted on. The first build had four 12 mm tubes of three points each at the corners of a straight-edged pyramid, which is why the single most recognisable feature of a spirit house was absent from the silhouette. Each of the four eave edges is now one 24 mm swept tube through seven stations: tip out and up, knee at the corner, a -22 mm dip at mid-span, mirrored. Two tube ends meet at every corner, which is correct -- the horn IS thicker than the fascia either side of it. The tips then taper 24 mm -> 7 mm over their last two stations: `tube` caps every segment, so a constant radius ends the horn in a flat disc and it rendered as four cut-off posts.

featureReviews.evidence: Body 0.425 x 0.415 (proxy bands 4-5 read 0.331 / 0.327 H; built 0.331 / 0.328-0.329, i.e. within 0.002). Gold #c8922a with #3a3e46 lattice plates on three faces, two doors with lattice on the front, dark-gold corner posts and plinth, verdigris grime canvas.
featureReviews.notes: Bands 4 and 5 were the worst two of the first build at -0.074 / -0.098 of H and are now the best two.

featureReviews.evidence: Octagonal moulded base, lathe radius 0.298 at seg 8 ry PI/8 so the flats land at 0.551 m; round stem to 0.335; two-tier slab, a 0.555 plinth to 0.415 then a 0.434 riser to 0.513. Bands 0-3 read -0.010 / -0.004 / +0.001 / +0.015.
featureReviews.notes: HD is a lathe RADIUS, not a width: at seg 8 with ry PI/8 the flats sit at HD*cos(22.5). Reading it as a width put the pedestal 0.062 m over its own envelope for one iteration.

name: Spirit House
nameTh: ศาลพระภูมิ
notes: A gilded miniature Chinese-Thai shrine house on a stone pedestal: octagonal moulded base, stem, square slab, square body with dark brick-lattice panels and a pair of doors, a flared hip roof with upturned corners, a smaller upper roof and a knob finial. One root pivot, no sockets, not breakable; box collider over the whole envelope. Declared size corrected 0.50 x 1.30 x 0.45 -> 0.63 x 1.30 x 0.62 at model time (2026-09-01). The proxy band table read the FIRST build under-width in all ten bands (mean |delta w| 0.0386, |delta d| 0.0523 of H) and the declared envelope was the reason: the proxy's widest band is 0.442 of H, i.e. 0.575 m, which a 0.50 m declaration cannot hold, and the model's own octagonal pedestal already measured 0.551 m across at band 0 -- outside the envelope it was declared in. The plate agrees: its eave tips span 592 px against the body's 400 and the object's 961 px of height, w/h 0.616, which at the plate's ~30 degree elevation is a true 0.53-0.54 against the declared 0.385. Height 1.30 is unchanged and remains the primary axis. Corrected a second time in the same session, from 0.58 to 0.63: 0.575 m is the proxy's widest BAND, which is the 5-95 percentile of the roof PLANE, and the upswept eave CORNERS stand outside it. A 4-segment roof lathe yawed 45 degrees puts its square's corners at the bbox extremes, so the horn tips add their outward run and their 24 mm fascia radius on top: built bounds are 0.6373 x 0.6219, declared 0.63 x 0.62. With that envelope the ten-band residual is mean |delta w| 0.0054 and |delta d| 0.0047 of H, every band inside 0.015 -- against 0.0386 / 0.0523 before.
